extracted.intended_audience: health communicators, emergency responders, and organizational leaders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and training materials for communicating about risks during public health emergencies; includes principles, trainings, and practical resources to help organizations convey lifesaving information. Focused on preparing communicators and leaders to design, test, and deliver messages across channels and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand and apply CERC principles and recommended practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction to CERC helps participants understand CERC principles and recommended practices and how applying them can help reduce harm during an emergency response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training includes in-depth practice on a variety of skills and techniques relevant to crisis and emergency risk communication. When virtual, the course is usually delivered over two consecutive days in four-hour sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the evidence-based CERC manual as the foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: The CERC manual provides an evidence-based framework and recommended practices for anyone who communicates on behalf of an organization responding to a public health emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual is the basis for all other CERC materials and trainings — consult it for core procedures, templates, and practice guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make information, products, and services accessible and understandable to intended audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop & Test Materials: Make information, products, and services accessible and understandable to intended audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iteratively develop and test materials with target audiences to ensure comprehension and usability during an emergency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply plain language principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops provide an overview of core CERC and plain language principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plain language in messages and materials to increase clarity and uptake; workshops include limited practice applying these concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for the psychology of a crisis when crafting messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Webinar topic: The Psychology of a Crisis — understand how people think and behave in crises to inform messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate research from public health and psychology to anticipate audience reactions, reduce fear, and encourage protective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define messages and tailor them to specific audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Webinar topic: Messages and Audiences — identify what to say and to whom during an emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Segment audiences and adapt content, tone, and channels so messages are relevant and actionable for each group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage community stakeholders in communication efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: Webinar topic: Community Engagement — involve community leaders and groups in planning and message dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage local partners to increase trust, reach, and cultural appropriateness of communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare and use designated spokesperson(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Webinar topic: Spokesperson — guidance on selecting and preparing spokespeople to represent organizations during emergencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train spokespeople on key messages, delivery, empathy, and coordination with response teams to maintain credibility and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select and coordinate appropriate communication channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Webinar topic: Communication Channels — choose channels that effectively reach intended audiences during an emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider traditional media, digital platforms, and community networks; coordinate timing and content across channels for consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use digital and social media strategically
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional Resource: Digital & Social Media — CDC uses a wide array of digital media tools to communicate important public health messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ social and digital tools to amplify messages, monitor public sentiment, and correct misinformation; adapt content for platform norms and audience behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide quick-reference tools for responders (wallet card)
rubrics_metrics.description: CERC Wallet Cards: The printable CERC wallet card summarizes CERC and is a quick reference for communicators during an emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make pocket-sized references available (attachable to a lanyard) and provide translations (English, Spanish, French) so responders can quickly consult core principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer tiered training formats to fit audience needs
rubrics_metrics.description: CERC training is offered in multiple formats: Introduction to CERC (full-day 8-hour), CERC for Leaders (half-day 4-hour), CERC Workshop (2–3 hours), and a 60-minute CERC Presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the training format based on audience role and time constraints: full-day for in-depth practice; shorter formats for leaders or overviews; 60-minute presentations for awareness-raising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train non-communicator leaders in the role of CERC
rubrics_metrics.description: CERC for Leaders is designed to help emergency response leaders who are not communication experts understand the role of CERC in reducing harm during emergencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concise, leader-focused content that emphasizes decision-making, messaging priorities, and how to work with communication teams.
